::: {.callout-note}
## About this page

A starting list of outside resources for learners: professional societies, journals, ready-made literature
searches, FDA device databases and companies in the field. Links lead to other websites, which this course does not
control. A listing is not an endorsement. Links were last checked on 2026-11-22; if one breaks, please report it
on the [Errata](errata.qmd) page.

Education only. Nothing here is for diagnosis, treatment or any clinical decision.
:::

details, and [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/) for broader discovery and "cited by" tracking.

### Search strings to adapt

Copy a string into PubMed and refine it with your own terms.

| Topic | PubMed search string | Run it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow challenges | `"electrophysiologist" AND "workflow challenges"` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22electrophysiologist%22+AND+%22workflow+challenges%22) |
| Mapping usability | `"electroanatomical mapping" AND usability` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22electroanatomical+mapping%22+AND+usability) |
| Manual annotation | `"local activation time" AND annotation AND variability` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22local+activation+time%22+AND+annotation+AND+variability) |
| Signal interpretation | `"intracardiac electrogram" AND interpretation AND limitations` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22intracardiac+electrogram%22+AND+interpretation+AND+limitations) |
| Mapping efficiency | `"high-density mapping" AND procedure time` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22high-density+mapping%22+AND+procedure+time) |
| Catheter navigation | `"catheter navigation" AND electrophysiology AND limitations` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22catheter+navigation%22+AND+electrophysiology+AND+limitations) |
| VT mapping | `"ventricular tachycardia" AND substrate mapping AND challenges` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ventricular+tachycardia%22+AND+substrate+mapping+AND+challenges) |
| AF mapping | `"atrial fibrillation" AND electrogram mapping AND workflow` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22atrial+fibrillation%22+AND+electrogram+mapping+AND+workflow) |
| PFA workflow | `"pulsed field ablation" AND workflow AND mapping` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22pulsed+field+ablation%22+AND+workflow+AND+mapping) |
| Radiation | `"electrophysiology laboratory" AND radiation exposure` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22electrophysiology+laboratory%22+AND+radiation+exposure) |
| Automation | `"electrophysiology" AND automated annotation` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22electrophysiology%22+AND+automated+annotation) |
| AI validation | `"electrophysiology" AND artificial intelligence AND validation` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22electrophysiology%22+AND+artificial+intelligence+AND+validation) |
| EP lab staffing | `"EP lab" AND staffing AND operational efficiency` | [Search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22EP+lab%22+AND+staffing+AND+operational+efficiency) |

## FDA device databases (United States)

| Resource | Use | Link |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FDA Medical Devices | Guidance, policy, safety communications and device information | [FDA portal](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices) |
| 510(k) database | Clearance records, device descriptions and predicate devices | [Search](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpmn/pmn.cfm) |
| PMA database | Premarket approvals and supplements | [Search](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm) |
| MAUDE | Reports of medical device adverse events | [Search](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfmaude/search.cfm) |
| Recalls and early alerts | Device recalls, corrections and removals | [FDA recalls](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/medical-device-safety/medical-device-recalls-and-early-alerts) |
| Product classification | Device class, regulation number and product code | [Search](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfPCD/classification.cfm) |
| Recognized consensus standards | Standards the FDA recognizes for device submissions | [Search](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfStandards/search.cfm) |
| Device Advice | How device regulation works, step by step | [FDA Device Advice](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/device-advice-comprehensive-regulatory-assistance) |
| ClinicalTrials.gov | Ongoing and completed clinical studies | [Search](https://clinicaltrials.gov/) |

How to read a device's public record:

1. Search by product name, manufacturer, model and product code.
2. Note the intended use, indications, contraindications and warnings.
3. Read the 510(k) summary or PMA record, and any supplements.
4. Check MAUDE reports and recall notices for safety signals worth a closer look.
5. Link each clinical study to the device and indication it actually tested.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read these records with care

A MAUDE report does not prove that a device caused an event. Reports can be incomplete, duplicated or unverified,
and raw counts do not compare device safety, because the number of devices in use is unknown. FDA clearance or
approval shows that a device met the regulatory standard; it does not, by itself, show that one device is better
than another.
:::

For how mapping systems are regulated, see
[m36 · From prototype to product](modules/m36-prototype-to-product.qmd); for AI software, see
[m45 · Evidence and regulation of AI in EP](modules/m45-ai-evidence-regulation.qmd).

## Social media

Societies and journals post news, papers and meeting coverage on X:
[\@HRSonline](https://x.com/HRSonline), [\@ESC_Journals](https://x.com/ESC_Journals) and
[\@ACCinTouch](https://x.com/ACCinTouch). Common EP hashtags include
[#EPeeps](https://x.com/search?q=%23EPeeps), [#CardiacEP](https://x.com/search?q=%23CardiacEP),
[#CardiacMapping](https://x.com/search?q=%23CardiacMapping) and [#PFA](https://x.com/search?q=%23PFA); searching X
needs a signed-in account.

Social posts are not peer-reviewed evidence. Note the author, date and original post, and look for a published
source before using a post to support a claim.

## Judging what you read

Three kinds of statement are easy to mix up, and they are not interchangeable:

1. a **reported frustration**: what users say is hard;
2. a **measured technical limit**: what a test or study measured;
3. a **validated clinical outcome**: what a clinical study showed for patients.

A simple way to label a source:

| Label | Source type |
| --- | --- |
| A · Formal evidence | Peer-reviewed study, consensus statement or official regulatory record |
| B · Reported need | Survey, structured interview or conference presentation |
| C · Company claim | Manufacturer material, product brochure or company announcement |
| D · Discovery signal | Social post, informal discussion or anecdote |

These labels are a reading aid, not a formal grading system such as GRADE.

When you cite a source:

- Prefer the original paper, society document, FDA record or instructions for use over a summary of it.
- Record the full title, authors, journal, year, DOI or PMID, and the date you accessed it.
- For a device, record the exact product name, model, software version, market and labeling version.
- For a comment from a clinician, record the role, context and date, and whether it is a personal view or a
  research finding.
- Do not infer how common a problem is from one interview or one post.
- Do not compare adverse-event counts without knowing how many devices were in use and how reports were made.
- Keep regulatory clearance, technical performance, clinical effectiveness and market adoption apart.
